2. The factual matrix of the case is that the accused entered into an agreement to sell and purchase of the property bearing municipal no. RZ 531A/25, Tughlakabad Extn. New Delhi consisting of basement, ground, first, second and third floor with terrace right measuring 50 sq yards forming part of Khasra no. 437 in the month of May 2010 vide advance receipt cum agreement to sell and purchase.

Accordingly, the accused received a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- in cash on 10.05.2010, Rs.
3,00,000/- on 17.05.2010 and Rs.3,00,000/- on 24.05.2010 and the balance amount of Rs.4,30,000/- was to be paid on or before 22.08.2010.
However in the meanwhile the son of the accused met with an accident and hence accused did not come forward to receive the balance amount despite repeated requests made by the complainant.
Not only that the accused refused to sell the above said property to the complainant.

In discharge of his obligation to pay the double of the received amount of Rs.9,00,000/- plus penalty, the accused issued two cheques bearing no.

However the said cheques returned unpaid on presentation with remark 'insufficient funds' vide return memos dated 05.10.2010.

In these circumstances, the plaintiff was constrained to send the legal notice dated 20.02.2007 at his correct address despite that the accused failed to make the payment within the statutory period of fifteen days.
Hence the criminal complaint u/s. 138 N I Act was filed by the complainant.
3. Upon service of summons, the accused put his appearance and notice was framed against him to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

After conclusion of trial and hearing final arguments,
the appellant was convicted for the offence under Section 138 N I Act IPC and punished for the same.
Aggrieved by said judgment, the present appeal has been filed by the appellant/accused.

GROUNDS OF APPEAL:
4. The impugned judgment has been challenged on the ground that the complainant failed to prove his complaint as well as transaction in question; that the complainant has failed to prove the alleged agreement to sell, alleged bayana receipt, cheques, return memos, legal notice and postal receipts;
that the accused had given six blank cheques to the complainant as security and there was no transaction between him and the complainant so as to constitute offence u/s. 138 N I Act; that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that though the accused admitted that he had issued cheque in question but stated that he had given six cheques instead of two cheques; that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that accused CA No. 204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. Yamin Khan & Anr. PAGE NO. 3 OF 16 has denied any liability in respect of cheques towards the complainant; that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the accused filed complaint u/s. 156(3) Cr.PC u/s. 420/468/471 IPC before the Ld. MM which is still pending; that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that ingredients of section 118(a) and section 139 of N.I. Act were lacking in the present case; that Ld.
Trial Court has erroneously presumed the liability against the appellant without any reason and corroboration of the evidence; that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the standard of proof to discharge the burden shifted on accused to rebut the presumption raised u/s. 139 N.I. Act is not the same as upon the prosecution to prove the case; that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the impugned cheques were misused by the complainant and the body of the cheque was duly filled-in by him to falsely implicate the accused in the present matter; that once it is proved that the legally enforceable liability existed, the presumption operates against the appellant at the time of issuing of the cheque and not prior to that; that the transaction itself is illegal and tainted with illegal object of the complainant and he cannot be given the advantage of his own wrong; that the Ld. Trial Court mechanically sentenced the appellant deciding all the issues; that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the complainant and accused were having family relations and later on complainant bore animosity against him; that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the complainant admitted that he has not filed any document except cheque in question in respect of the alleged transaction; that though the accused admitted his signature CA No. 204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. Yamin Khan & Anr. PAGE NO. 4 OF 16 on the cheque but denied of having issued the same and Ld. Trial Court failed to consider that there must be legally enforceable debt fortified by the Jiauddin vs Yamin Khan And Anr on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71922566/
2 admitted transaction between the parties which is not the case in hand; that the Ld. Trial Court wrongly shifted the burden of proving the case upon the accused instead of the complainant; that the impugned judgment was passed in mechanical manner without application of judicial mind.

5. Notice of the present appeal was issued to the respondent.
However, no reply was filed on his behalf and addressed oral arguments.
6. It was argued by the ld. Counsel for the respondent
Thus, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
7. I have heard the Ld. Counsel for appellant as well as respondent and perused the record of the Trial Court as well as the impugned judgment.
8. Before proceeding further let us go through the relevant provisions of law.

The main ingredients of Section 138 of the CA No. 204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. Yamin Khan & Anr. PAGE NO. 6 OF 16 Negotiable Instruments Act are as follows:
(a) The accused issued a cheque on an account maintained by him with a bank.
(b) The said cheque has been issued in discharge of any legal debt or other liability.

sentences.text: (c) The cheque has been presented to the bank within the period of six months from the date of the cheque or within the period of its validity.
(d) When the aforesaid cheque was presented for encashment, the same was returned unpaid/dishonoured.
(e) The Payee of the cheque issued a legal notice of demand within 30 days from the receipt of information by him from the Bank regarding the return of the cheque.
(f) The Drawer of the cheque failed to make the payment within 15 days of the receipt of the aforesaid legal notice of demand.
If the aforesaid ingredients are satisfied then the drawer of the cheque shall be deemed to have committed an offence punishable u/s 138 Negotiable Instruments Act.
8.1 Under Section 139 of the NI Act, unless the contrary is proved, the holder of a cheque shall be presumed to have received the cheque in discharge of any debt or other liability.
Sub clause (a) of Section 118 of the NI Act, inter-alia provides that unless the contrary is proved, a drawn up negotiable instrument, if accepted, has to be presumed to be for consideration.

In Goa Plast (P) Ltd.
vs. Chico Ursula D'souza & Anr., (2003) 3 SCC 232, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the provisions of Section 138 to 142 of the NI Act, is for the purpose of giving credibility to negotiable instruments in business transactions.

sentences.text: In view of the same it becomes an admitted fact that it was the accused who signed at point A and B on the alleged cheques Ex.CW1/B and Ex.CW1/C but the point of contention raised from the side of the accused that he handed over the blank cheques to the complainant and apart from the cheques he also handed over blank stamp paper and another blank paper to him.
He has further submitted that the other details of the cheque were filled by the complainant and strongly rebuts that the cheques were issued in discharge of his liability.

The said contention is going against the own stand of the accused who has admitted of taking loan of Rs.2,00,000/-from the complainant and also claimed to issue six cheques given qua the security of the said loan.
Here the question which arises is that whether the accused has repaid the said loan and has not explained why he issued six cheques qua the said loan.
Was it towards any monthly installment or towards the interest is not clear.

In order to prove his defence, accused examined himself as DW-2 and he has deposed that "My son met with an accident in May 2010; that after that period of five days he was shifted to my residence; that when he was shifted home, a number of people had come to ask about his wellness; that the complainant had also come home to inquire about my son's illness; that the complainant offered monetary help as assistance as I was in need of money; that I was in CA No. 204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. Yamin Khan & Anr. PAGE NO. 9 OF 16 need of money as such I accepted his offer; that the complainant gave me Rs. Two Lakhs by way of cash; that I had given him six blank cheques and one stamp paper in blank and also one blank plan paper signed by me; that I had given the said cheques and stamp paper and plane paper as security; that the complainant used to provide finance assistance to the people on interest basis; that there was no talks for the sale of said property where I was residing. "

Assuming the defence taken by the accused as true then where comes the need of giving chain of his property documents pertaining to previous ownership to the complainant after putting his signatures or photocopy of his title deed to the complainant as admitted by the accused in his cross-examination.
Here also accused took the plea that he delivered the same to the complainant as security for advance of Rs.2,00,000/- taken by him.
Isn't it quite surprising that for a loan of Rs.2,00,000/-
accused
has handed over not only six blank signed cheques but also title documents of the property worth Rs.40,00,000/- as deposed by DW-6 Shabnam and DW-7 Irshad Ahmad.
Secondly , accused has not only admitted his signatures on the cheques but also admitted his signature at point D cancelling the revenue stamp affixed on the said agreement to sell.
From perusal of the said agreement to sell it cannot be said that the same was signed without any content on it.
The signature of the appellant does not appear to be out of the box as apparent from the sign on the cancelled stamp.
Further it has also been signed by the witnesses which also seems to be in place.

Not only did DW-1 handed over chain of his property documents pertaining to previous ownership to CA No. 204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. Yamin Khan & Anr. PAGE NO. 10 OF 16 the complainant after putting his signatures or photocopy of his title deed to the complainant but also handed over signed copies of his election card, ration card, driving license and PAN card as admitted during cross-examination and he has no explanation to give as to how those documents reached the complainant.

It is further alleged by the complainant that he paid Rs. 9 lakh to the accused and thereafter he refused to sell the aforesaid property to the complainant and in terms of the agreement issued the two impugned cheques towards penalty.
The accused has admitted his signatures on all the aforesaid documents.
The accused has stated that the aforesaid documents were handed over in blank to complainant which has been misused by the complainant.
It is seen from the perusal of the advance cum agreement to sell and purchase Ex. CW1/A that it has been duly attested by two witnesses.

But none of the aforesaid witnesses have been examined by the defence in order to show that Ex.
CW1/A already contained the signatures of the accused and the contents of the same were filled up by the complainant as is the defence taken by the accused; that further the accused has been unable to explain how the complainant got in possession of all the authorised CA No. 204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. PAGE NO. 11 OF 16 Identification proofs as well as the residential proofs of the accused which are Mark A (Colly) and it is pertinent to mention here that all the copies of the aforesaid documents have been self- attested by the accused himself and he has not denied his signatures on the same."
8.3
Thirdly , the accused took the defence that he took loan of Rs.2,00,000/- from the complainant at the time when his son namely Javed Mansoori i.e. DW-4 was in hospital due to an accident.

However during cross examination he has stated that his son was discharged from the hospital 4-5 days after his admission but he has not filed any medical document i.e. admission ticket or discharge summary to prove the same.
In order to prove the said defence, accused has examined DW-1 Nasiruddin, DW-3 Jishan Khan, DW-4 Javed Mansoori and DW-5 Babuddin.
Out of those witnesses, DW-3 has deposed that he came to know that complainant advanced sum of Rs.2,00,000/- to the accused which means that he was not the eye witness to the said fact.

DW-4 has deposed that his father took sum of Rs.2,00,000/- from the complainant since "his father was in financial embarrassment due to losses in his business" but he failed to explain the losses suffered by his father.

DW-1 has deposed that against the loan of Rs.2,00,000/- accused handed over two papers out of which one was blank and other was stamp paper and six blank cheques whereas DW-5 has deposed that accused signed and delivered one affidavit, one plain paper and six cheques to the complainant in order to secure the repayment of the loan.

According to the son of accused i.e. DW-4 his father took the loan due to losses whereas DW-5 has stated in cross examination that accused was CA No. 204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. Yamin Khan & Anr. PAGE NO. 12 OF 16 running factory of readymade garments from his house and was earning adequately.

The accused has been unable to show what serial number of cheques were allegedly handed over by him to the complainant.
No documentary evidence has been placed on record in this regard."

9. During course of arguments it was submitted by the ld. counsel for the appellant that complainant has failed to prove his financial capacity and has relied on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Raja Ram Vs. Maruthachalam 2023 AIR SC 471.

sentences.text: " The point to be noted herein that though during the course of arguments the ld. counsel for the appellant challenged the financial capacity of the complainant however accused himself has deposed that complainant used to provide financial assistance to the people on interest basis.
In that situation how it can be said that the complainant has no financial capacity to lend such a huge amount to him.

Secondly , though accused asked the questions from the complainant about his annual income and complainant also admitted that he did not reveal the alleged transaction of Rs.9,00,000/- to the accused in his income tax return during his cross examination but no such specific plea was raised during the trial and no specific suggestion was put from the side of the accused regarding the financial capacity of the complainant to lend money.
Hence the Ld. Trial Court did not give any finding regarding the financial capacity of complainant to lend money.

The whole line of defence of the accused revolved around the plea that he never entered into any agreement to sell his property CA No. 204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. Yamin Khan & Anr. PAGE NO. 14 OF 16 with the complainant which he has failed to prove during the course of trial.

sentences.text: The accused has failed to rebut the presumption u/s. 139 of the N.I. Act which says that cheque duly drawn was towards a debt or liability.

It has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in K.N. Beena vs. Muniyappan and Another (2001) 8 SCC 458 that "in view of the provisions of Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act read with Section 118 thereof, the Court had to presume that the cheque had been issued for discharging a debt or liability.

entities.text: K.N. Beena vs. Muniyappan and Another (2001) 8 SCC 458

sentences.text: The said presumption was rebuttable and could be rebutted by the accused by proving the contrary.
But mere denial or rebuttal by the accused was not enough.
The accused had to prove by cogent evidence that there was no debt or liability."
The accused has failed to prove that he has no debt or liability towards the complainant rather he has admitted taking of loan of Rs.2,00,000/- from him.

10. In view of the aforesaid discussion, I find no illegality or material irregularity in the impugned judgment and order on sentence dated 05.06.2014 passed by Ld. Trial Court.

There is no CA No.
204120/2016 Jiauddin Vs. Yamin Khan & Anr. PAGE NO. 15 OF 16 valid ground for interference with the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant and the present appeal deserves to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
